Subject: Mapping pricing options for expanding usage — MedalTech

Hi Kimberly,

We’re planning to ramp up our usage starting in July — roughly a 2.5x increase in inference hours for our primary service over the next 6 months. Our current contract runs through 2026-12-31 and was provisioned as an annual committed package. Procurement asked me to check with you on the cleanest path to add capacity without blowing out our renewal timeline.

High-level asks:
- Can you share options for adding capacity mid-contract (pro-rate vs. short-term committed add-on)?
- Any standard concession you offer for incremental committed units during a scaling window?
- If we re-benchmark to co-term the new capacity with our existing December renewal, how would you typically handle pricing and credits?

Procurement needs an indicative quote and PO path by 2026-06-18 to keep our onboarding timeline. I’ve attached the current contract and a short usage export.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-minute call if that helps.

Best,
Samuel Ortiz
Head of Platform
MedalTech

Hi Samuel — thanks for the context and the attachment. High level we can take three pragmatic paths; I’ve sketched the tradeoffs below and attached a quick worksheet that pulls estimated unit economics based on the usage you sent.

Option A — Short-term committed add-on (fastest)- Add a committed block that starts immediately, pro-rated to calendar month, priced at incremental rate (no change to base contract term). Advantage: simplest for procurement and quick to approve. Drawback: higher incremental unit price vs. annualize.

Option B — Staged co-term annualize (recommended if growth sustains)- Convert a portion of the incremental usage into a committed uplift that co-terms to 2026-12-31. We apply a partial voucher credit for previously-unused seat/commitation, then repriced blended rate across the new total. Advantage: better unit economics; Drawback: requires legal amendment and co-term billing alignment.

Option C — Consumption true-up + volume concession (flex)- Keep usage on pay-as-you-go, but we offer a temporary incremental discount band for the first 90 days (e.g., -15% off incremental token units) while we observe patterns, then decide to convert to A or B. Advantage: lowest friction; Drawback: less predictability for you and for forecasting.

Estimated next steps I suggest:
1) If Procurement needs a PO by 6/18, we can provision Option A immediately and include a 90-day conversion clause to Option B if you decide to annualize.
2) If MedalTech is comfortable with legal amendment timelines, we can prepare an Option B amendment and a blended quote — that usually takes Legal + Procurement 5–10 business days.

I attached: pricing_scenarios.xlsx (quick model) and a one-pager of the three options. I’ll loop in Ben on the pricing concession and Jordan for procurement sequencing.

Would you like a short call today at 2pm PT?

—Kimberly

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: MedalTech — recommended concession for scaling window

Kimberly/Jordan — quick internal note following Sam’s ask. I ran the numbers in the attached workbook and my recommendation to protect gross margin while accelerating procurement is:

- Offer a 15% discount on incremental committed units for the first 90 days (applies only to delta above the committed baseline).
- If they convert to co-term annualized commit within 90 days, convert the 90-day discount into a one-time voucher equal to the dollars discounted (credited on the first invoice after amendment).
- Add SLA carveout: if they need guaranteed latency tiers for specific routes, we can attach a limited SLA with a capacity buffer (extra monthly fee).

Rationale: keeps the PO path simple for procurement (we can ship Option A with a short clause), preserves our ability to annualize at a better rate later, and provides a clear credit mechanism for Finance.

Jordan — can you confirm Legal/Finance tolerance on voucher conversion and whether we need exec approval for the 15% concession at this deal size? Est. revenue impact for the concession is low relative to 12-month ARR upside.

—Ben
Senior Account Executive
From: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@medaltech.com>

Thanks Kimberly — that framing helps. Procurement is happy with Option A if we can get a quote + PO path by 6/18. A few clarifying items before we lock:

1) Please include the 15% timebound incremental discount in the quote (applies to July–Sept usage).
2) We need a clear conversion mechanic written into the SOW (if we annualize within 90 days the discount converts to a credit toward the first invoice of the amended term).
3) Can you confirm whether the voucher/credit is refundable or only applied against future invoices? (Procurement prefers applied-credit vs. cash refund).

If that’s all straightforward we’ll issue the PO. We’ll sign quickly if DocuSign is available — procurement is out of the office next week, so speed matters.

—Sam
